Sufficiency claims (Experiment 3) based only on 2nd-order Markov processes; generalization to natural text structure and realistic architectures unclear

Methodologically rigorous progression from natural to semi-natural to synthetic data with multiple metrics (PS, LA, AR) and cross-validation (R²=0.76-0.94), strengthening causal inferences
Precise operationalization of frequency and reliability that improves upon prior 'burstiness' concept with formal definitions and clear Pareto frontier characterization
Comprehensive experimental documentation including hyperparameters, statistical details, controlled data generation algorithms, and honest limitations discussion

weaknesses: Predictive law lacks mechanistic explanation—coefficients (-0.37, -0.62) and constant T≈750,000 are empirically derived via regression on 35 models without principled theoretical grounding or explanation for why these values arise

Experiment 3 findings show contradictions not adequately addressed: -D conditions produce IHs with high repetition when measured by LA/AR metrics (Appendix J.3), directly contradicting the claim that 'local dependency is necessary,' relegated to a footnote

Limited model scope undermines generalizability: most experiments use 2-layer 50M GPT2 models, only trained on 1B tokens (single epoch), English-only data; unclear if findings transfer to modern LLMs with different architectures/scales

Experiment 2 Pareto frontier has fuzzy rather than sharp boundaries, and asymmetry between [i,j] and [j,i] cells suggests the semi-natural data generation does not fully decouple frequency and reliability properties

Primarily descriptive rather than mechanistic: while characterizing WHEN IHs form and WHAT data properties matter, the paper provides limited insight into WHY these properties matter or how they connect to transformer learning dynamics

Methodological concerns: piecewise linear regression with 3 segments (Appendix D.1) lacks sensitivity analysis; PWLF fitting on 30 checkpoints could spuriously identify emergence points; no validation against perturbations

Missing critical ablations: no testing across tokenizers despite acknowledging subword inflation effects, no architecture generalization beyond GPT2/Pythia, no analysis of vocabulary size effects on claimed universal properties

weaknesses: Paper is descriptive rather than explanatory: no mechanistic insight into why specific scaling exponents (β=-0.37, γ=-0.62) arise; functional form not justified against alternatives

Severe scope limitations undermine generalizability: models trained only to 350M (largest inference 7B), single task (next-token prediction), single tokenizer (GPT2 subword, which 'inflates repeated bigrams'), single language/domain
Unclear practical significance: paper predicts when IHs emerge but doesn't establish why this matters—no connection to downstream performance, training decisions, or capability improvements
